selection.rationale: The requested objective is step_ms (max across ranks; original baseline 136.86/137.05 ms). Composition of one accumulated step, from measured evidence: non-NCCL compute kernels total ~34.0 ms for all 4 micro-batches (nsys rank-0 trace spans the complete accumulate: 8 embedding gathers, 13 NCCL kernels, ends at the loss stack), while the 13 DDP bucket allreduces cost ~61.8 ms when measured cleanly (collective_calibration: 28,351,488 B -> 3.52 ms median, 157,541,376 B -> 19.50 ms; 12x3.52+19.5). Exposure: after the first collective kernel starts, only 8.49 ms of compute remains in the final backward and 1.73 ms after the last starts, so communication is essentially fully serialized at the step tail; overlap with compute cannot be increased further inside the frozen no_sync schedule. The wire path is NCCL RING_LL over SHM/direct (peer_access 0 in both directions, NVLink unsupported, 2 channels) at a logical 8.05 GB/s for both payload sizes, while device telemetry during the comm window shows pcie.tx ~7.3 GB/s and pcie.rx ~8.5 GB/s, i.e. the LL-protocol path, not the link, appears to set the ~62 ms floor (PCIe/SHM saturation estimate for the 497,759,232 B per-rank gradient payload is ~40 ms). These 13 collectives are the only collectives in the step (payload coverage 13/13 observed) and are jointly owned by exactly two eligible call groups at the shared c10d.allreduce_.default dispatch boundary: f833b57a373d8262a384 (call d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 invocations of the 7,087,872-element bucket shape) and 8525af72c631b94e3dd0 (call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, the single 39,385,344-element embedding bucket). Bucket membership spreads across all layer groups, so no per-layer group independently owns communication cost; conversely, faster local compute kernels (mm 10.5 ms, addmm 4.8 ms inclusive) cannot move step_ms materially while ~45% of the step is exposed communication. A replacement must cover both payload shapes at this one boundary, so the two groups are selected as a joint candidate. Constraints preserved: same worker-initialized process group, async_op=True Work semantics, in-place float32 SUM into the gradient_as_bucket_view bucket tensors, no DDP configuration/bucketing change and no comm hook; DDP's own world-size division and the frozen step boundary stay untouched. Per-element the reduction remains a single two-addend sum (commutative), so results are bitwise identical to NCCL's ring sum, keeping the exact cross-rank replica check (atol=0/rtol=0), the full-global-batch gradient reference check and the parameter check unchanged, and the diagnostic communication goal only improves.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the bucket allreduce dispatch at both selected call groups with a bandwidth-optimized two-rank reduction on the existing NCCL process group - e.g. a chunked one-shot exchange that splits each bucket into large contiguous halves, exchanges them with point-to-point sends/receceptions so both directions move SIMPLE-protocol bulk transfers, adds each half locally, and swaps the reduced halves back into the bucket view; or any equivalent path that lifts effective throughput above the observed 8.05 GB/s RING_LL ceiling - will shorten the ~62 ms serialized tail communication toward the ~40 ms link-saturation estimate and reduce step_ms by roughly 10-20 ms (~8-15%), because communication is measured to be almost fully exposed (only 8.49 ms of overlap available) and is the largest single block of the 137 ms step. Bitwise-identical gradient values (two-addend commutative sum, DDP still divides by world size) preserve every quality check including exact cross-rank equality. This is a hypothesis to be tested: if the 8 GB/s LL result already reflects the SHM/PCIe hard ceiling for this pair, or if chunking adds launch overhead comparable to the bandwidth gain, measured step_ms will not improve and the candidate must be rejected on measurement; expected benefit is not acceptance.

proposal.rationale: Implements the joint selection (groups f833b57a373d8262a384 and 8525af72c631b94e3dd0) at the single shared c10d.allreduce_.default boundary that jointly owns all 13 bucket collectives of the step. Repair of trial-b0a02885e2 using the measured feedback. (1) The concrete failure: every one of the 13 replacement invocations routed parent:guard_reduce_op because the dispatcher passes the reduce op as a torch.ScriptObject wrapping __torch__.torch.classes.c10d.ReduceOp whose op() returns plain integer 0, while torch._C._distributed_c10d.RedOpType is not importable at top level in this worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129 (the enum is nested as type(ReduceOp.SUM)); the P2P exchange therefore never executed and its performance has never been measured. The repaired guard positively identifies SUM from the boxed form only when the script class identity matches the c10d.ReduceOp custom class and the value converts through the RedOpType enum and equals SUM (arbitrary integers are never accepted), verified on the measured worker's Python on CPU: torch.classes.c10d.ReduceOp().op() -> 0, int(ReduceOp.SUM) == 0, type(ReduceOp.SUM)(0) == ReduceOp.SUM. The op's ProcessGroup argument is likewise a ScriptObject and resolves through ProcessGroup.unbox (the form the prior run already passed on its way to the reduce-op guard). (2) The implementation takes the selection hypothesis's explicitly permitted 'equivalent path': instead of host-orchestrated isend/irecv rounds (two host-ordered rounds plus a local add per bucket, whose two-rank gloo rehearsal also showed backend-dependent tag-matching fragility), each flat fp32 bucket's SUM allreduce on the same worker-initialized NCCL process group is decomposed into async reduce_scatter_single(scratch_half, bucket, SUM) followed by async all_gather_single(bucket, scratch_half), both enqueued back-to-back with no host wait between them: NCCL executes collectives issued on one process group in issue order on the group's single device stream, so the allgather is device-ordered after the reduce-scatter, and the returned allgather Work (boxed via work.boxed(), the same return convention torch's own c10d meta registrations use) covers the whole exchange, preserving the parent op's async ABI exactly. Wire volume per rank is unchanged at S bytes, the information-theoretic minimum for an exact allreduce (identical to the ring), and every output element is a single two-addend commutative fp32 add computed on exactly one rank and then copied, so results are bitwise identical across ranks and to the parent SUM; DDP's world-size division happens before this boundary and is untouched. Validated end-to-end on the worker's Python with a CPU/gloo harness at both observed shapes (7,087,872 and 39,385,344 elements, repeated invocations exercising the persistent scratch): results bitwise equal to the parent allreduce op, exact cross-rank equality, parent:guard_size and parent:guard_signature fallbacks executing the parent correctly, and route labels split_allreduce on all supported calls; the gloo branch takes an explicit wait because gloo lacks issue-order execution, while the guarded production path is nccl-only. (3) How the feedback changes this attempt's expectation: the previous candidate was in effect a passthrough ablation - 13 parent calls, byte-identical outputs (max_abs_error 0.0), zero scratch, P2P never run - and still measured 230.5/234.1 ms against parent 131.0/139.1 ms. That +91 to +100 ms is the cost of installing any functional replacement at this unscoped boundary under the legacy binding backend (a global dispatch mode entered for the whole measured invocation, taxing every ATen dispatch of forward, backward and optimizer), and it exceeds the ~62 ms total communication these 13 collectives can influence; even a zero-cost collective cannot recover it, so step_ms improvement is not expected unless that overhead was specific to conditions this bundle changes. This repair makes the selected hypothesis actually executable so the framework's paired AB/BA measurement can decide it on evidence; expected benefit is not acceptance.

setup_work.build_time: No model or parameter transforms, no CUDA work, no new process groups, no comm hooks, no environment changes. build() creates two replacement closures over context['references'] and one per-device scratch cache; installation measured ~4-7 ms in the prior trial and adds no allocation beyond the closure dict.
setup_work.runtime_lazy: The first supported invocation allocates one persistent float32 scratch of numel/2 elements sized for the largest observed bucket (19,692,672 elements = 75.0 MiB for the 39,385,344-element embedding bucket; the 7,087,872-element buckets reuse a prefix slice). The allocation happens once per worker during the first (warmup) invocation and the buffer is retained for the process lifetime, so the caching allocator never races multi-stream reuse; first-use NCCL reduce-scatter/allgather path warmup also lands in warmup invocations.
setup_work.per_call_work: Two async collective enqueues on the process group's NCCL stream (reduce_scatter_single then all_gather_single), no host wait between them on the nccl path, no local add, no chunking, no tags, and a Work.boxed() return. The engine thread is never blocked, matching the parent op's async structure.
setup_work.memory_impact: Steady state retains +75.0 MiB allocated scratch, visible in framework.peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle counters; no per-invocation growth; no CUDA Graphs or retained graph pools. This is a documented setup/retained allocation, not a general physical-memory saving.

quality_risks: Measured binding overhead dominates: the prior trial's all-parent-fallback execution with byte-identical outputs (max_abs_error 0.0, 13 parent:guard_reduce_op routes) measured 230.5/234.1 ms against parent 131.0/139.1 ms, i.e. ~+95 ms from the legacy functional binding itself (a global dispatch mode active for the whole measured invocation). That exceeds the ~62 ms total communication at these sites, so the paired project measurement will most likely reject this candidate on objective_not_improved unless the overhead was specific to conditions this bundle changes; this is disclosed, not assumed, and acceptance belongs to the framework's AB/BA protocol.

Exactness: every output element is one two-addend commutative fp32 add computed on exactly one rank (the ring reduce-scatter owner of that half) and then copied, so the atol=0/rtol=0 cross-rank replica check holds structurally and values are bitwise equal to the parent SUM; validated bitwise against the parent allreduce op on the worker's Python with a CPU/gloo harness at both observed shapes. DDP's pre-boundary world-size division is untouched, so the reference-gradient (1e-6/1e-4) and post-step parameter checks are unaffected.

The chained async reduce-scatter -> allgather relies on NCCL executing collectives issued on one process group in issue order on the group's single device stream; the CPU/gloo harness lacks that guarantee (it takes an explicit wait and showed corruption without it), so the no-wait branch is production-nccl-only by guard. If the ordering assumption were violated on the worker, gradients would mismatch the single-GPU reference comparison loudly (1e-6/1e-4 per-parameter check) rather than pass silently; a hang would surface as a timeout, never as silent corruption.

The returned Work is the final allgather handle boxed with work.boxed() (the same mechanism torch's own c10d meta registrations use at this op's return position). Because both stages share the process group's NCCL stream and the allgather is enqueued last, its completion covers the entire exchange; DDP-side wait/getFuture on a genuine Work handle is preserved.

Divergent rank routing would hang rather than corrupt: every guard is a pure function of rank-identical inputs (bucket shape/dtype/layout, backend, world membership, reduce op), fallbacks happen strictly before any enqueue, and post-enqueue exceptions propagate instead of triggering a parent fallback (a parent call after a partial exchange would double-reduce the bucket).

The op's timeout argument is not forwarded (the Python collective API accepts no per-call timeout); the process group's default timeout governs both stages, matching the parent's timeout=-1 default behavior.

The workload's second, non-requested diagnostic goal (diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms, measured in separate profiled invocations with a step_ms<=1.05x baseline constraint) counts NCCL AllReduce kernel time; this replacement substitutes ReduceScatter/AllGather kernels, so that diagnostic becomes non-comparable while the requested step_ms objective is unaffected.

Route telemetry: fallback labels distinguish setup failures (parent:setup_process_group, parent:setup_backend, parent:setup_ranks), unsupported signatures (parent:guard_device/dtype/layout/size/backend/world_size/reduce_op/sparse_indices/tensor_list/signature, parent:error_<Type> for pre-enqueue exceptions) and the executed path (split_allreduce); labels are diagnostic self-report only.
Retained +75.0 MiB scratch raises warm-run peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle counters; reported explicitly rather than described as a saving.

usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

recovery.scope: All interrupted GPU measurements excluded from this decision; full original validation repeated

external_invariants: Model architecture is frozen: GPT2Config(n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024) with resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager', FP32 weights via .float(), .train() mode, initialized under torch.manual_seed(20261020); no pretrained weights are downloaded (assets is empty by design, seeded synthetic fixtures are the task data).

Inputs are frozen: per-rank synthetic token IDs from torch.randint(0, 50257, (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128)) repeated accumulation_steps=4 times using torch.Generator().manual_seed(31000 + rank).

Workload dimensions are frozen: world_size=2, micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4; effective batch 8 and 1024 tokens per step; the first 3 micro-batch backwards run under DDP.no_sync() and only the final micro-batch backward triggers the gradient all-reduce.
Numerical policies are frozen: TF32 disabled for cuBLAS matmul and cudnn, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark False, torch num_threads=4 and num_interop_threads=1, seed 20261020.

DDP configuration is frozen: broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True; no communication hook and no profiler on the measured path (the source's bucket-inventory hook belongs to a separate diagnostic and is never installed).

Optimizer semantics are frozen: torch.optim.SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False); optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) executes inside the timed step (never pre-cleared in reset); each micro-batch loss is model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / accumulation_steps and the accumulated loss is the sum over micro-batches.

Quality contract preserved from the source: finite accumulated loss; full per-parameter gradient comparison against the single-GPU full-global-batch reference with grad_atol=1e-6/grad_rtol=1e-4; exact cross-rank gradient equality with atol=0.0/rtol=0.0; post-step parameter comparison with parameter_atol=1e-6/parameter_rtol=1e-4; the +1-corruption negative control. The adapter exposes loss, every gradient and every updated parameter and leaves the comparisons to the framework; no accuracy or convergence is claimed beyond these reference-fidelity checks.

Objective semantics are frozen: step_ms is each rank's wall time of the complete accumulated step with the source's final torch.cuda.synchronize() as the completion boundary, aggregated as max across ranks; work is never moved out of the timed step to improve the score and no fabricated sub-metrics or sub-phase objectives are introduced.

The adapter uses context['device'] and the worker-initialized process group exclusively; it never picks a physical GPU, never initializes another default process group, never destroys a process group, and performs no CUDA work at import time.
